message.content:
I’m not able to pull live traffic data, but I can give you the most common “fastest‑looking” routes that most navigation apps (Google Maps, Waze, Apple Maps, etc.) will recommend under normal conditions.

| Option | Typical Route | Approx. Distance | Approx. Drive Time (no heavy traffic) |
|--------|---------------|------------------|---------------------------------------|
| **1 – I‑95 N** | New York → I‑95 N → I‑84 N (via Hartford) → I‑90 N → I‑93 N → Boston | ~215 mi (346 km) | ~3 h 30 min |
| **2 – I‑84 N (via Hartford)** | New York → I‑84 N → I‑91 N → I‑93 N → Boston | ~210 mi (338 km) | ~3 h 45 min |
| **3 – I‑87 N → I‑90 N** | New York → I‑87 N → I‑90 N → I‑93 N → Boston | ~220 mi (354 km) | ~3 h 55 min |

### Why I‑95 N is usually the “fastest” choice
- **Directness**: It’s the most direct interstate corridor between the two cities.
- **High‑capacity**: I‑95 is a major north‑south artery with multiple lanes and frequent service areas.
- **Traffic patterns**: While it can get congested near the NYC metro area and around the Boston‑area interchange, it typically has fewer long‑haul truck stops than I‑84.

### Things to keep in mind
- **Traffic**: Rush hour (Mon‑Fri 7–9 am & 4–6 pm) can add 30–60 min, especially near the NYC and Boston metropolitan areas.
- **Construction**: Check a real‑time map or your navigation app for any lane closures or detours.
- **Weather**: Winter storms can slow traffic dramatically on I‑95; I‑84 may be a better alternative if snow is forecast.

### Quick tip
If you’re looking for the *current* fastest route, open your preferred navigation app (Google Maps, Waze, Apple Maps) and let it calculate the best path based on live traffic. It will also suggest alternate routes if a major incident occurs.

Enjoy your trip!
